featured_reviews.name: Sagar Mungekar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Deeply mourned with the sad demise of my stray
One month ago I had sent a post wherein I posted how IDA saved my stray dog, but today I am posting again as the dog died on Sunday afternoon 4/06/23, Some issues I felt are important to share so posting, After bringing back the dog fell ill within 15 days.This time her hemoglobin was only 1, I medicated her as directed by the doctors at my home then also the levels dropped, so after a week I admitted her again, I was charged 2000/- for it even though I paid 3500/- in first instance.  Saving the dog was more imp than amount so I paid without any complaint or issue, again after 15 days she got discharged the doctors said that she is keeping good health and her haemoglobin level have gone to 8, seeing her health I was not convinced but the doctor insisted saying you can't keep as she is better now, if they would have kept for 4-5 days more she could have definitely recovered properly but the doctor denied to keep. One consulting doctor comes on 3 days on Tues, wed & Thursday but he said to take her back on Monday itself so i had to discharge her. From Wednesday she stopped to eat at all so i called up in IDA emergency services number, But they directed me to samast Mahajan but things did not work from them too, I tried to contact the visiting doctor, but in vain I feel if just if she could direct me on phone itself things would have worked but it didn't happen.
If at all IDA authorities see this message I would request that please do not discharge any pet or stray till it gets really well because we are ignorant about how to deal with the situation. I strongly feel that the doctors in hospital should be more responsible as for us and for strays you are next to god so please take care, please don't ignore animals saying they are trying to run away or they come to bite as this is expected from pets/ strays without doubt, also as the fortification is too strong so they can't run away , as well as the ground staff under them is good so they get good support from them, the people in management or the trustees should look into this issues more strictly as it is matter of life or survival of those animals who can't talk & are totally dependent.
Again with joined hands Irequest all the pet lovers please ensure that the pet or stray is completely well before discharging him/ her. IDA authorities also please consider my request & take my post positively I have lost my dog but it may be of help for others. IDA has the ability to strive for animal welfare so please please dont miss this god gif To maintain that they have to be at mark, the doctors are the saviours & they must act accordingly. Somewhat bad  & disappointing experience this time, sorry to say.

After reading this, if you still want to keep your pet with him, pls do so at your own risk.

featured_reviews.review_text: My beautiful, playful 3 year old kitty Koko suffered from a severe spinal injury unbeknownst to me with her symptoms showing up in the beginning of May. It had caused her to become paralyzed in her hind legs and she was as a result unable to use her litterbox or walk. She was unable to apply pressure of any kind using her lower half due to disk compression/herniation as diagnosed by the vets at Tata Trust small animal hospital. I was told that she may never walk again and that I should consider putting her down due to concerns regarding her quality of life with her being unable to poop or pee on her own. I was heart broken for my little girl and felt defeated. A day later I found out about Dr. Deepa Katyal's clinic and wasted no time in starting her treatment there. Dr. Deepa and her expert staff handled our case with so much love, care and dedication which helped Koko regain the strength in her legs within a week. After a month of daily treatments consisting of phototherapy and electroacupuncture Koko feels brand new and is back to being her usual energetic and mischievous self. I feel such relief as I watch her chase her little brother around the house and use the litterbox all on her own with ease just like she used to. I am eternally grateful to Dr. Deepa Katyal and her incredible staff for helping my Koko recover so miraculously and their selfless commitment to the cause of animal pain management. Needless to say Dr. Deepa Katyal's clinic is my go to for addressing any concerns regarding both of my cats. If any of you are in a similar situation, my heart goes out to you; Dr. Deepa Katyal's Animal Wellness and Rehabilitation Centre will take care of your pet and you♡

featured_reviews.name: Muskaan Arora
featured_reviews.review_text:
One of the best and genuine animal welfare NGOs I’ve come across. I discovered them in 2021 and have seen them grow tremendously over time. What makes them truly special is their team - including school and college students, working professionals, and dedicated animal lovers across age groups, all coming together for a common cause.

I’ve had the opportunity to closely work with the team, and their dedication is truly commendable. Animal welfare isn’t easy, it involves making tough and critical decisions but they continue to give their best and often go out of their way to help animals. Truly inspiring work!

featured_reviews.name: richa sharma
featured_reviews.review_text:
A heartfelt thank you to Founder Sushank and CAP Organisation for giving this sweet soul the better life she truly deserved. From severe skin infection to healing and hope, Mili’s transformation (before and after pic) says it all. She is a street dog near our apartment, and today she has a new chance at life. Every soul on the streets deserves love, dignity, and care, and CAP continues to serve this cause in every way they can.

This is not the only case they have helped us with—they have supported 2–3 more dogs as well, always stepping in selflessly. They never asked us for donations for treatment, but we felt it was our responsibility to contribute and support such genuine work.

Requesting everyone to please support them in whatever way possible. They may not have big backing, but they have big hearts. ♥️

featured_reviews.name: Meera Pathak
featured_reviews.review_text:
A 12-year-old dog from my college had a uterine prolapse, and when no one else responded or was ready to help, CAP Foundation immediately stepped in. They took her in, made sure she got the surgery she needed, and cared for her through the entire recovery.

name: The Pets Planet
description: We are a non-profit, no kill shelter for all breeds of dogs and cats. We are a caring stray and pet animals shelter situated right 9n the cost of Manori Jetty Malad west. Founded in June 2002, we rescue and care for homeless animals. Most of the dogs and cats that we take in are from high kill facilities that are euthanizing due to lack of space. Many have been abused, neglected or abandoned . Once rehabilitated and ready, they are carefully matched with prospective adopters and placed in loving homes. We do take in some owner relinquishments as well and there are a variety of reasons people give up their dog or cat to us. The most common reasons are lack of time due to a change in work schedule, moving, allergies, new baby etc.
